Prerequisites: None
Description: Exposes freshmen and new transfer undergraduate students to current topics of U.W. research in chemistry. Students interface with research groups. Includes a "big picture" description of the scientific goals and main questions of the highlighted group along with a discussion of experimental methods. Credit/no-credit only.

Course: CHEM 197 - Science Outreach Training
Credits: 1-2, max. 2
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Training as a peer mentor for General Chemistry or for participation in science-related outreach activities to the community. Not applicable toward chemistry degree requirements. Credit/no-credit only.

Course: CHEM 220 - Principles of Chemistry II
Credits: 5
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 120, CHEM 142, or CHEM 143. Offered: W.
Description: Second course in a three-quarter overview of general chemistry, organic chemistry, and biochemistry. Not for students majoring in biochemistry, chemistry, or engineering. Introduction to organic chemistry including organic compounds, functional groups, stereochemistry, and basic organic reactions. Course overlaps with: CHEM 223; CHEM 237; CHEM 257; and B CHEM 237. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 120, CHEM 142, or CHEM 143. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 221 - Principles of Chemistry III
Credits: 5
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 1.7 in CHEM 220. Offered: Sp.
Description: Third course in a three-quarter overview of general chemistry, organic chemistry, and biochemistry. Not for students majoring in biochemistry, chemistry, or engineering. Introduction to biochemistry including biomolecular structure, proteins, nucleic acids, biochemical cycles, and cellular energetics. Course overlaps with: CHEM 224; CHEM 239; CHEM 259; and B CHEM 239. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 1.7 in CHEM 220. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 223 - Organic Chemistry - Short Program
Credits: 4
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 152, CHEM 153, or CHEM 155. Offered: AS.
Description: First of a two-quarter series. Not for biochemistry or chemistry majors and may not be accepted by professional schools that require organic chemistry. Introduction to structure, nomenclature, properties, and reactions of organic compounds with a focus on alkenes, alkynes, and alkyl halides. Stereochemistry and spectroscopy. Course overlaps with: CHEM 220; CHEM 237; CHEM 257; and B CHEM 237. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 152, CHEM 153, or CHEM 155. Offered: AS.

Course: CHEM 224 - Organic Chemistry - Short Program
Credits: 4
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 1.7 in CHEM 223. Offered: WS.
Description: Continuation of CHEM 223. Structure, nomenclature, properties, and reactions of aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acid derivatives, amines, carbohydrates, lipids, amino acids, peptides, proteins, and nucleic acids. No laboratory accompanies this course, but CHEM 241 laboratory may be taken concurrently. Course overlaps with: CHEM 221; CHEM 239; CHEM 259; and B CHEM 239. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 1.7 in CHEM 223. Offered: WS.

Course: CHEM 237 - Organic Chemistry
Credits: 4
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165. Offered: AWSpS.
Description: First course for students planning to take three quarters of organic chemistry. Introduction to physical properties, structure, nomenclature, and stereochemistry of organic compounds. Reactions of alkenes and alkynes. No organic laboratory accompanies this course. CHEM 237; CHEM 238; and CHEM 239 (or equivalents) must be completed in sequence. Course equivalent to: B CHEM 237. Course overlaps with: CHEM 220; CHEM 223; CHEM 257; and T CHEM 251. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: CHEM 238 - Organic Chemistry
Credits: 4
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 237 or CHEM 257. Offered: AWSpS.
Description: Second course for students planning to take three quarters of organic chemistry. Further discussion of physical properties and transformations of organic molecules, especially aromatic compounds, and spectroscopy of organic molecules. CHEM 237; CHEM 238; and CHEM 239 (or equivalents) must be completed in sequence. Course equivalent to: B CHEM 238. Course overlaps with: CHEM 258. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 237 or CHEM 257. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: CHEM 239 - Organic Chemistry
Credits: 4
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 238 or CHEM 258. Offered: AWSpS.
Description: Third course for students who take three quarters of organic chemistry. Further discussion of physical properties and transformations of organic molecules, especially carbonyl compounds and amines. Polyfunctional compounds and biological polymers including carbohydrates, amino acids, proteins, and nucleic acids. CHEM 237; CHEM 238; and CHEM 239 (or equivalents) must be completed in sequence. Course equivalent to: B CHEM 239. Course overlaps with: CHEM 221; CHEM 224; CHEM 259; and T CHEM 271. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 238 or CHEM 258. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: CHEM 241 - Organic Chemistry Laboratory
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 223, CHEM 237, or CHEM 257; and a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 224, CHEM 238, or CHEM 258, any of which may be taken concurrently. Offered: AWSpS.
Description: Introduction to organic laboratory techniques. Synthesis, purification, and spectroscopic analysis of representative compounds. Designed to be taken with CHEM 224 or CHEM 238. Course equivalent to: B CHEM 241. Course overlaps with: CHEM 261. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 223, CHEM 237, or CHEM 257; and a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 224, CHEM 238, or CHEM 258, any of which may be taken concurrently. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: CHEM 242 - Organic Chemistry Laboratory
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum 1.7 grade in either CHEM 241 or CHEM 261; a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 223, CHEM 238, or CHEM 258; and a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 224, CHEM 239 (which may be taken concurrently), or CHEM 259 (which may be taken concurrently). Offered: AWSpS.
Description: Preparations and qualitative organic analysis. Designed to be taken with CHEM 239. Course equivalent to: B CHEM 242. Course overlaps with: CHEM 262. Prerequisite: a minimum 1.7 grade in either CHEM 241 or CHEM 261; a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 223, CHEM 238, or CHEM 258; and a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 224, CHEM 239 (which may be taken concurrently), or CHEM 259 (which may be taken concurrently). Offered: AWSpS.

Course: CHEM 257 - Honors Organic Chemistry
Credits: 4
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165. Offered: A.
Description: For chemistry majors and otherwise qualified students planning three or more quarters of organic chemistry. Structure, nomenclature, reactions, and synthesis of organic compounds. Theory and mechanism of organic reactions. Studies of biomolecules. No organic laboratory accompanies this course. Course overlaps with: CHEM 220; CHEM 223; CHEM 237; and B CHEM 237. Prerequisite: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 258 - Honors Organic Chemistry
Credits: 4
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 2.2 in CHEM 257. Offered: W.
Description: For chemistry majors and otherwise qualified students planning three or more quarters of organic chemistry. Structure, nomenclature, reactions, and synthesis of organic compounds. Theory and mechanism of organic reactions. Studies of biomolecules. Course overlaps with: CHEM 238 and B CHEM 238. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.2 in CHEM 257. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 259 - Honors Organic Chemistry
Credits: 4
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 2.2 in CHEM 258. Offered: Sp.
Description: For chemistry majors and other qualified students. Structure, reactions, and synthesis of organic compounds. Discussion of physical properties and transformations of molecules such as enols, enolates, amines, and phenols. Polyfunctional compounds and biological polymers (e.g., carbohydrates, amino acids, proteins, and nucleic acids). Course overlaps with: CHEM 221; CHEM 224; CHEM 239; and B CHEM 239. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.2 in CHEM 258. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 261 - Honors Organic Chemistry Laboratory
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 1.7 in CHEM 257; and a minimum grade of 1.7 in CHEM 258, which may be taken concurrently. Offered: W.
Description: Introduction to organic laboratory techniques. Preparation, purification, and analytical characterization of organic compounds. Designed to be taken with CHEM 258. Course overlaps with: CHEM 241 and B CHEM 241. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 1.7 in CHEM 257; and a minimum grade of 1.7 in CHEM 258, which may be taken concurrently. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 262 - Honors Organic Chemistry Laboratory
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 1.7  in CHEM 258; a minimum grade of 2.2 in CHEM 261; and a minimum 1.7 grade in CHEM 259, which may be taken concurrently. Offered: Sp.
Description: Synthetic preparation and qualitative analysis of organic molecules and biomolecules. Designed to accompany CHEM 259. Course overlaps with: CHEM 242 and B CHEM 242. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 1.7  in CHEM 258; a minimum grade of 2.2 in CHEM 261; and a minimum 1.7 grade in CHEM 259, which may be taken concurrently. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 291 - Study Abroad - Chemistry
Credits: 1-15, max. 15
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: For student in the UW study abroad program. Content varies and is individually evaluated. Credit does not apply to major degree requirements without departmental approval.

Course: CHEM 297 - Science Outreach Participation
Credits: 1/2, max. 6
General Education: 
Prerequisites: CHEM 197
Description: Serve as an experienced peer mentor for general Chemistry or as an experienced outreach volunteer. Not applicable toward chemistry degree requirements. Prerequisite: CHEM 197
Credit/no-credit only.

Course: CHEM 312 - Inorganic Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; and either CHEM 223, CHEM 237, or CHEM 257. Offered: AWS.
Description: Introduces principles of inorganic chemistry and its broader relevance in society. Emphasis on bonding, physical properties, and reactivity of transition metal complexes. Prerequisite: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; and either CHEM 223, CHEM 237, or CHEM 257. Offered: AWS.

Course: CHEM 317 - Inorganic Chemistry Laboratory
Credits: 4
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 165 or CHEM 312; and either CHEM 242, CHEM 262, or B CHEM 242. Offered: WSp.
Description: Experimental exploration of the periodic table. Techniques of preparation and characterization of inorganic compounds. Prerequisite: either CHEM 165 or CHEM 312; and either CHEM 242, CHEM 262, or B CHEM 242. Offered: WSp.

Course: CHEM 321 - Quantitative Analysis
Credits: 5
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165. Offered: AWSp.
Description: Introduction to quantitative chemical analysis, including gravimetric, volumetric, spectrophotometric, and potentiometric analysis, as well as chemical separations and data analysis. Includes laboratory. Course overlaps with: B CHEM 316. Prerequisite: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165. Offered: AWSp.

Course: CHEM 416 - Transition Metals
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 165 or CHEM 312; and either CHEM 223, CHEM 237, or CHEM 257; recommended: CHEM 312. Offered: A.
Description: Survey of selected key topics in the chemistry of the transition metals, including emphasis on the structure, bonding, and reactivity of major classes of compounds. Prerequisite: either CHEM 165 or CHEM 312; and either CHEM 223, CHEM 237, or CHEM 257; recommended: CHEM 312. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 417 - Inorganic Reaction Mechanisms
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 224, CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239; and CHEM 312. Offered: Sp.
Description: Overview of the reactivity of transition metal complexes, including experimental techniques to deduce reaction mechanism. Highlights applications in organic synthesis and catalysis. Prerequisite: either CHEM 224, CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239; and CHEM 312. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 418 - Nuclear Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 453, CHEM 455, or CHEM 475. Offered: W.
Description: Natural radioactivity, nuclear systematics and reactions, radioactive decay processes, stellar nucleosynthesis, applications of radioactivity. Prerequisite: either CHEM 453, CHEM 455, or CHEM 475. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 422 - Analytical Spectroscopy
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: CHEM 321; and CHEM 455 or CHEM 475, either of which may be taken concurrently. Offered: A.
Description: Qualitative and quantitative analysis of molecular species, using various optical spectroscopy techniques including absorption, fluorescence, Raman, and advanced nonlinear optical spectroscopy. Prerequisite: CHEM 321; and CHEM 455 or CHEM 475, either of which may be taken concurrently. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 425 - Meso and Microfluidics in Chemical Analysis
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165.
Description: Covers chemical, biological, and medical applications of micro- and mesofluidics. Topics include fundamentals, droplet-based microfluidics, cell based assays and 'organ on a chip' models, analytical methods using microfluidics, open microfluidics, and microfabrication/surface chemistry. Prerequisite: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165.
Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 426 - Instrumental Analysis
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: CHEM 321. Offered: W.
Description: Introduction to modern instrumental methods of chemical analysis, including chromatography, optical and mass spectroscopy, electrochemistry and flow injection analysis. Basic concepts of transducers, spectrometers, mass analysis, separation sciences, and computerized data acquisition and reduction. Includes laboratory. Prerequisite: CHEM 321. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 427 - Data Science for Chemical Measurements
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; recommended: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165. Offered: A.
Description: Explores the intersection of chemistry and data science, examining how data-intensive methods and artificial intelligence transform chemical measurement, analysis, and discovery. Addresses what constitutes data in chemical research, challenges unique to analyzing chemical measurements, and foundational data science skills applied to authentic chemical problems. No prior programming experience necessary. Prerequisite: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; recommended: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 428 - Biomolecular Analysis
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either BIOC 405, BIOC 440, or CHEM 321 Offered: Sp.
Description: Principles of identifying and quantifying biological molecules, including metabolites, proteins, and nucleic acids, using modern analysis techniques, including analytical spectroscopy, molecular recognition, mass spectrometry, and separations. Emphasis on bioinformatics as well as the role of chemical measurements in medical diagnostics and biomedical research. Includes laboratory. Prerequisite: either BIOC 405, BIOC 440, or CHEM 321 Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 429 - Chemical Separation Techniques
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 224, CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239; and either CHEM 241, CHEM 321, CHEM 261, or B CHEM 241. Offered: W.
Description: Introduction to modern separation techniques such as gas chromatography, high-performance liquid chromatography, electrophoresis, and field flow fractionation. Prerequisite: either CHEM 224, CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239; and either CHEM 241, CHEM 321, CHEM 261, or B CHEM 241. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 430 - Advanced Physical Organic Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239. Offered: A.
Description: Fundamental aspects of organic structures and transformations with an emphasis on frontier molecular orbital theory and arrow-pushing mechanisms. Structure and reactivity of carbocations, addition reactions, substitution reactions, elimination reactions, structure and reactivity of anions, electrophilic substitutions, neighboring group effects, conformational analysis, pericyclic reactions, and single-electron chemistry. Prerequisite: either CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 431 - Advanced Synthetic Organic Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: CHEM 430. Offered: W.
Description: Discussion of modern organic reactions and their mechanisms and their application to the synthesis of various organic compounds, including pharmaceuticals, materials, and natural products. Selectivity in complex molecules, carbon-nitrogen and carbon-carbon bond forming reactions, metal-catalyzed reactions, organocatalysis, and other modern synthetic techniques and strategies. Prerequisite: CHEM 430. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 432 - Advanced Bio-Organic Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239; and CHEM 242 or CHEM 262. Offered: Sp.
Description: Fundamental aspects of the structure, function, and synthesis of biological molecules. Enzyme mechanisms with an emphasis on cofactor-dependent and redox catalysis, and applications of biological catalysts in organic synthesis. Biological synthesis of complex organic molecules. Application of chemical methods to the study of biological processes. Prerequisite: either CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239; and CHEM 242 or CHEM 262. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 434 - Polymer Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239. Offered: Sp.
Description: Focuses on the fundamental and applied aspects of polymer chemistry with a particular focus on polymer structure, synthesis, and self-assembly. Topics include classic methods and mechanisms for macromolecular synthesis and contemporary breakthroughs in the field and the applications of polymers and their societal impact. Prerequisite: CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 435 - Polymer Physics
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: M E 323. Offered: jointly with M E 409.
Description: Dives into the statistical-mechanical, thermodynamic, and continuum theories that describe the structure, dynamics, and rheology of polymeric materials. Focuses on developing a deep conceptual understanding of the theoretical frameworks and simulation methods used in polymer research and connecting these to experimental methods. Teaches techniques to analyze and predict the behavior of specific polymer systems. Prerequisite: M E 323. Offered: jointly with M E 409.

Course: CHEM 436 - Chemical Biology
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 224, CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239; recommended: either BIOC 405 or BIOC 440 Offered: W.
Description: Mechanistic enzymology and chemical biology. Topics include protein structure and function, how enzymes work as catalysts, kinetic methods, functional assays, and applications to current research. Prerequisite: either CHEM 224, CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239; recommended: either BIOC 405 or BIOC 440 Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 441 - Data Science and Materials Informatics
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduction to data science approaches and their applications to materials science research.  Basic skills in data mining, data processing, and machine learning for materials research topics using Python taught through case studies and other methodologies. Recommended: prior programming experience; some experience with Python helpful. Offered: jointly with MSE 477; A.

Course: CHEM 442 - Materials and Device Modeling
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: MSE 477/CHEM 441. Offered: jointly with MSE 478.
Description: Implementation of computational and data science methods in materials science discovery and device modeling to gain physical and statistical insights of materials design.  First-principles methods, multiscale simulations, and continuum modeling will be introduced within the framework of active machine learning with application of both computational and data science methods to materials study. Prerequisite: MSE 477/CHEM 441. Offered: jointly with MSE 478.

Course: CHEM 443 - Big Data for Materials Science
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: MSE 477/CHEM 441. Offered: jointly with MSE 479.
Description: Introduces the challenges and opportunities of the big data era for materials science and chemistry research.  Students will gain basic knowledge and skills of data management using high performance computing, including automated data processing, batch processing, and cloud based computational tools that are suitable for materials science research. Prerequisite: MSE 477/CHEM 441. Offered: jointly with MSE 479.

Course: CHEM 452 - Thermodynamics and Kinetics for Biochemists
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; MATH 126 or MATH 136; and PHYS 116 or PHYS 123. Offered: AWS.
Description: Chemical thermodynamics and kinetics emphasizing biochemical applications. Course overlaps with: CHEM 456 and B CHEM 401. Prerequisite: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; MATH 126 or MATH 136; and PHYS 116 or PHYS 123. Offered: AWS.

Course: CHEM 453 - Quantum and Statistical Mechanics for Biochemists
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: CHEM 452 or CHEM 456; MATH 126 or MATH 135; and PHYS 116 or PHYS 123. Offered: WSpS.
Description: Advanced topics in physical chemistry including quantum mechanics, statistical mechanics, spectroscopy, kinetics, and transport, emphasizing biochemical applications. Course overlaps with: CHEM 455; CHEM 457; CHEM 475; and B CHEM 402. Prerequisite: CHEM 452 or CHEM 456; MATH 126 or MATH 135; and PHYS 116 or PHYS 123. Offered: WSpS.

Course: CHEM 454 - Introduction to Biomolecular Spectroscopy
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: CHEM 452 or CHEM 456; either CHEM 453 or CHEM 455. Offered: Sp.
Description: Introduction to biomolecular spectroscopy. Covers optical and magnetic resonance time-domain spectroscopies, single-molecule methods, etc., with applications to the structure and dynamics of proteins, nucleic acids, biomembranes, and biomaterials. Prerequisite: CHEM 452 or CHEM 456; either CHEM 453 or CHEM 455. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 455 - Quantum Mechanics of Atoms and Molecules
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; MATH 126 or MATH 136; and PHYS 116 or PHYS 123. Offered: ASp.
Description: Foundations of quantum mechanics and applications to atoms and molecules and their spectra. Course overlaps with: CHEM 453; CHEM 475; and CHEM E 456. Prerequisite: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; MATH 126 or MATH 136; and PHYS 116 or PHYS 123. Offered: ASp.

Course: CHEM 456 - Chemical Thermodynamics
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; MATH 126 or MATH 136; and PHYS 116 or PHYS 123. Offered: WS.
Description: Chemical thermodynamics. Laws of thermodynamics presented with applications to phase equilibria, chemical equilibria, and solutions. Course overlaps with: CHEM 452. Prerequisite: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; MATH 126 or MATH 136; and PHYS 116 or PHYS 123. Offered: WS.

Course: CHEM 457 - Statistical Mechanics of Atoms, Molecules, and Materials
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: CHEM 455 or CHEM 475; and either CHEM 452, CHEM 456, or CHEM E 326. Offered: SpS.
Description: Introduction to statistical mechanics, kinetic theory, transport, and chemical kinetics. Course overlaps with: CHEM 453. Prerequisite: CHEM 455 or CHEM 475; and either CHEM 452, CHEM 456, or CHEM E 326. Offered: SpS.

Course: CHEM 458 - Air Pollution Chemistry
Credits: 4
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Global atmosphere as a chemical system emphasizing physical factors and chemical processes that give rise to elevated surface ozone, particulate matter, and air toxics; international issues of air pollution transport and changing tropospheric background composition; and regulatory control strategies and challenges. Aimed at science and engineering majors. Course overlaps with: B CHEM 350. Offered: jointly with ATMOS 458; A.

Course: CHEM 460 - Spectroscopic Molecular Identification
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 224, CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239. Offered: A.
Description: Basic theory of spectral techniques - infrared spectroscopy, NMR, and mass spectrometry - with emphasis on spectral interpretation skills needed for the elucidation of structure, conformation, and dynamics in organic and biological chemistry. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 1.7 in either CHEM 224, CHEM 239, CHEM 259, or B CHEM 239. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 461 - Physical Chemistry Laboratory
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: one of the following: (1) CHEM 453; (2) CHEM 455 and CHEM 456; (3) CHEM 475; recommended: prior computer programming experience or coursework at the level of CSE 121 or CSE 160. Offered: AW.
Description: Physical measurements in chemistry. Vacuum techniques, calorimetry, spectroscopic methods, kinetics, use of computational tools to simulate or model data and determine experimental errors. Prerequisite: one of the following: (1) CHEM 453; (2) CHEM 455 and CHEM 456; (3) CHEM 475; recommended: prior computer programming experience or coursework at the level of CSE 121 or CSE 160. Offered: AW.

Course: CHEM 462 - Techniques of Synthetic Organic Chemistry
Credits: 2/3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 242, CHEM 262, or B CHEM 242; and CHEM 460, which may be taken concurrently. Offered: A.
Description: Laboratory techniques of synthetic organic chemistry. Vacuum distillation, multistep synthesis, air sensitive reagents, photochemistry, chromatography, and separation techniques. Prerequisite: either CHEM 242, CHEM 262, or B CHEM 242; and CHEM 460, which may be taken concurrently. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 463 - Spectroscopic Techniques for Structural Identification
Credits: 2
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: CHEM 460. Offered: W.
Description: Laboratory techniques of spectroscopic analysis for structural determination and molecular interaction of small molecules using UV, IR, NMR, and mass spectrometry. Prerequisite: CHEM 460. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 464 - Computers in Data Acquisition and Analysis
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 453, CHEM 455, or CHEM 475; and either MATH 136, or MATH 207 and MATH 208. Offered: Sp.
Description: Introduction to use of the computer in the chemistry laboratory. Principles of microcomputers and their use for such problems as data acquisition, noise reduction, and instrument control. Prerequisite: either CHEM 453, CHEM 455, or CHEM 475; and either MATH 136, or MATH 207 and MATH 208. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 465 - Computational Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: CHEM 455 or CHEM 475. Offered: W.
Description: Basics of molecular quantum chemistry (Hartree-Fock and density functional theory); numerical implementation using computers, including basics of programming and scientific computing; applications to problems in chemistry; use of computational chemistry software packages to study chemical reactions and molecular properties. Prerequisite: CHEM 455 or CHEM 475. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 466 - Energy Materials, Devices, and Systems
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: either PHYS 431, E E 421, MSE 311, MSE 312, MSE 313, MSE 351, MSE 352, CHEM E 456, CHEM 455, or CHEM 475, any of which may be taken concurrently. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 440/MSE 466/PHYS 466; A.
Description: Provides project-based training for synthesis and characterization of new energy materials for generation and storage and integrating renewables into energy systems. Employs instruments at the Clean Energy Research Training Testbeds, a UW user facility. Topics include nanoparticle synthesis, solar cell and module characterization, coin cell battery assembly and testing, photochemistry, 2D semiconductors, and grid simulation. Prerequisite: either PHYS 431, E E 421, MSE 311, MSE 312, MSE 313, MSE 351, MSE 352, CHEM E 456, CHEM 455, or CHEM 475, any of which may be taken concurrently. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 440/MSE 466/PHYS 466; A.

Course: CHEM 475 - Honors Quantum Mechanics of Atoms and Molecules
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; MATH 126 or MATH 136; and PHYS 116 or PHYS 123. Offered: A.
Description: Origins and basic postulates of quantum mechanics, solutions to single-particle problems, angular momentum and hydrogenic wave functions, matrix methods, perturbation theory, variational methods. Covers quantum mechanics at greater depth than CHEM 455. Course overlaps with: CHEM 453 and CHEM 455. Prerequisite: either CHEM 153, CHEM 162, or CHEM 165; MATH 126 or MATH 136; and PHYS 116 or PHYS 123. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 484 - Electronic and Optoelectronic Polymers
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 453, CHEM 455, or CHEM 475. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 484/MSE 484; A.
Description: Covers the chemistry, physics, materials science, and applications of semiconducting and metallic conjugated polymers. Examines the structural origins of the diverse electronic and optoelectronic properties of conjugated polymers. Exemplifies applications by light-emitting diodes, lasers, solar cells, thin film transistors, electrochromic devices, biosensors, and batteries. Prerequisite: either CHEM 453, CHEM 455, or CHEM 475. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 484/MSE 484; A.

Course: CHEM 485 - Electronic Structure and Application of Materials
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: CHEM 455 or CHEM 475; recommended: familiarity with particle in a box; free electron model; symmetry and symmetry elements; molecular orbital theory; principles of inorganic chemistry; and ability to independently research and learn advanced topics. Offered: W.
Description: Introduction to electronic structure theory of solids from a chemical perspective, including band theory and the free electron model, with an emphasis on modern trends in research in inorganic materials in the bulk and on the nanometer scale. Prerequisite: CHEM 455 or CHEM 475; recommended: familiarity with particle in a box; free electron model; symmetry and symmetry elements; molecular orbital theory; principles of inorganic chemistry; and ability to independently research and learn advanced topics. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 486 - Electronic Dynamics in Organic and Inorganic Materials
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either CHEM 453, CHEM 455, CHEM 475, PHYS 324, or CHEM E 456. Offered: Sp.
Description: Energy and charge transfer; exciton migration and charge transport; photophysical dynamics in optoelectronic and kinetic processes in electrochemical energy conversion. Prerequisite: either CHEM 453, CHEM 455, CHEM 475, PHYS 324, or CHEM E 456. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 491 - Study Abroad - Advanced Chemistry
Credits: 1-15, max. 15
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: For students in the UW study abroad program. Content varies and is individually evaluated. Credit does not apply to major degree requirements without departmental approval.

Course: CHEM 499 - Undergraduate Research
Credits: 1-10, max. 35
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Research in chemistry. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: CHEM 500 - Grant Proposal and Scientific Writing
Credits: 1
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduces steps in compiling a successful grant proposal and writing scientific articles, personal statements, research summaries, and procuring recommendation letters, using the NSF graduate fellowship as a guide. Students gain experience in peer review processes as assessment of current scientific literature. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 501 - Readings in Chemistry
Credits: 1, max. 9
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Individual meetings with faculty to discuss readings (journal articles, book chapters, proceedings) in the chemical sciences. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: CHEM 508 - Advanced Inorganic Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduction to physical inorganic chemistry.  Topics include group theory, ligand-field theory, and various physical methods for understanding the properties of open-shell metal ions, including vibrational spectroscopies (IR and Raman), electronic absorption spectroscopy, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, and magnetism. Recommended: familiarity with basic quantum mechanics and statistical thermodynamics; symmetry and symmetry elements; and transition-metal chemistry; and ability to independently research and learn advanced topics. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 510 - Current Problems in Inorganic Chemistry
Credits: 3, max. 9
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Primarily for doctoral candidates in inorganic chemistry. Current topics (e.g., bioinorganic, advanced organometallic, materials and solid state, advanced inorganic spectroscopy). See department for instructor and topics during any particular quarter. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 516 - Transition Metals
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Survey of selected key topics in the chemistry of the transition metals, including emphasis on the structure, bonding, and reactivity of major classes of compounds. Recommended: working knowledge of general chemistry and introductory inorganic concepts including Lewis structures, metal-ligand coordination, and oxidation state assignments. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 517 - Inorganic Reaction Mechanisms
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: CHEM 416 or equivalent background. Offered: W.
Description: Overview of the reactivity of transition metal complexes, including experimental techniques to deduce reaction mechanism. Highlights applications in organic synthesis and catalysis. Prerequisite: CHEM 416 or equivalent background. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 521 - Analytical Electrochemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Theory and practice of modern electrochemistry with emphasis on instrumentation and applications in chemical analysis.

Course: CHEM 522 - Analytical Spectroscopy
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: CHEM 321; and CHEM 455 or CHEM 475, either of which may be taken concurrently.  Offered: W.
Description: Qualitative and quantitative analysis of molecular species, using various optical spectroscopy techniques including absorption, fluorescence, Raman, and advanced nonlinear optical spectroscopy. Prerequisite: CHEM 321; and CHEM 455 or CHEM 475, either of which may be taken concurrently.  Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 523 - Geochemical Cycles
Credits: 4
General Education: 
Prerequisites: permission of instructor. Offered: jointly with ATMOS 508/OCEAN 523.
Description: Descriptive, quantitative aspects of earth as biogeochemical system. Study of equilibria, transport processes, chemical kinetics, biological processes; their application to carbon, sulfur, nitrogen, phosphorus, other elemental cycles. Stability of biogeochemical systems; nature of human perturbations of their dynamics. Prerequisite: permission of instructor. Offered: jointly with ATMOS 508/OCEAN 523.

Course: CHEM 524 - Analytical Mass Spectrometry
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Theory and practice of mass spectrometry with emphasis on ionization methods, mass analyzers, gas-phase ion chemistry, and spectra interpretation. Recommended: basic knowledge of organic and physical chemistry, including thermodynamics and kinetics. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 525 - Meso and Microfluidics in Chemical Analysis
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Covers chemical, biological, and medical applications of micro- and mesofluidics. Topics include fundamentals, droplet-based microfluidics, cell based assays and 'organ on a chip' models, analytical methods using microfluidics, open microfluidics, and microfabrication/surface chemistry. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 526 - Instrumental Analysis
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduction to both fundamental theory and instrument design of various analytical instruments. Focuses on four major categories of instrumental analysis methods: optical spectroscopy, chromatography, flow injection analysis, and electroanalytical chemistry. Beyond learning basic analytical principles and instrument design, students receive extensive laboratory training in all major analytical methods. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 527 - Data Science for Chemical Measurements
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Explores the intersection of chemistry and data science, examining how data-intensive methods and artificial intelligence transform chemical measurement, analysis, and discovery. Addresses what constitutes data in chemical research, challenges unique to analyzing chemical measurements, and foundational data science skills applied to authentic chemical problems. No prior programming experience necessary. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 528 - Biomolecular Analysis
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Principles of quantifying and identifying biological molecules, including metabolites, proteins, and nucleic acids, using modern analysis techniques, including analytical spectroscopy, molecular recognition, mass spectrometry, and separations. Emphasis on bioinformatics, the role of chemical measurements in medical diagnostics and biomedical research, and the primary literature. Includes laboratory. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 529 - Chemical Separation Techniques
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduction to modern separation techniques such as gas chromatography, high-performance liquid chromatography, electrophoresis, and field flow fractionation. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 530 - Advanced Physical Organic Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Fundamental aspects of organic structures and transformations with an emphasis on frontier molecular orbital theory and arrow-pushing mechanisms. Structure and reactivity of carbocations, addition reactions, substitution reactions, elimination reactions, structure and reactivity of anions, electrophilic substitutions, neighboring group effects, conformational analysis, pericyclic reactions, and single-electron chemistry. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 531 - Advanced Synthetic Organic Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: CHEM 530. Offered: W.
Description: Discussion of modern organic reactions and their mechanisms and their application to the synthesis of various organic compounds, including pharmaceuticals, materials, and natural products. Selectivity in complex molecules, carbon-nitrogen and carbon-carbon bond forming reactions, metal-catalyzed reactions, organocatalysis, and other modern synthetic techniques and strategies. Prerequisite: CHEM 530. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 532 - Advanced Bio-Organic Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Fundamental aspects of the structure, function, and synthesis of biological molecules. Enzyme mechanisms with an emphasis on cofactor-dependent and redox catalysis, and applications of biological catalysts in organic synthesis. Biological synthesis of complex organic molecules. Application of chemical methods to the study of biological processes. Recommended: CHEM 536. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 534 - Polymer Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Focuses on the fundamental and applied aspects of polymer chemistry with a particular focus on polymer structure, synthesis, and self-assembly. Topics include classic methods and mechanisms for macromolecular synthesis and contemporary breakthroughs in the field and the applications of polymers and their societal impact. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 535 - Polymer Physics
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Dives into the statistical-mechanical, thermodynamic, and continuum theories that describe the structure, dynamics, and rheology of polymeric materials. Focuses on developing a deep conceptual understanding of the theoretical frameworks and simulation methods used in polymer research and connecting these to experimental methods. Teaches techniques to analyze and predict the behavior of specific polymer systems. Offered: jointly with M E 509.

Course: CHEM 536 - Chemical Biology
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Mechanistic enzymology and chemical biology. Topics include protein structure and function, how enzymes work as catalysts, kinetic methods, functional assays, and applications to current research. Recommended: either BIOC 405 or BIOC 440. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 541 - Data Science and Materials Informatics
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduction to data science approaches and their applications to materials science research.  Basic skills in data mining, data processing, and machine learning for materials research topics using Python taught through case studies and other methodologies. Recommended: prior programming experience; and some experience with Python helpful.   Offered: jointly with MSE 542; A.

Course: CHEM 542 - Materials and Device Modeling
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: either MSE 477/CHEM 441, MSE 542/CHEM 541, CHEM E 545/CHEM 545/MSE 545, or CHEM E 546/CHEM 546/MSE 546 (or equivalents). Offered: jointly with MSE 543.
Description: Implementation of computational and data science methods in materials science discovery and device modeling to gain physical and statistical insights of materials design.  First-principles methods, multiscale simulations, and continuum modeling will be introduced within the framework of active machine learning with application of both computational and data science methods to materials study. Prerequisite: either MSE 477/CHEM 441, MSE 542/CHEM 541, CHEM E 545/CHEM 545/MSE 545, or CHEM E 546/CHEM 546/MSE 546 (or equivalents). Offered: jointly with MSE 543.

Course: CHEM 543 - Big Data for Materials Science
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: either MSE 477/CHEM 441,  MSE 542/CHEM 541, or both CHEM E 545/MSE 545/CHEM 545 and CHEM E 546/MSE 546/CHEM 546. Offered: jointly with MSE 544; Sp.
Description: Introduces the challenges and opportunities of the big data era for materials science and chemistry research.  Students will gain basic knowledge and skills of data management using high performance computing, including automated data processing, batch processing, and cloud based computational tools that are suitable for materials science research. Prerequisite: either MSE 477/CHEM 441,  MSE 542/CHEM 541, or both CHEM E 545/MSE 545/CHEM 545 and CHEM E 546/MSE 546/CHEM 546. Offered: jointly with MSE 544; Sp.

Course: CHEM 545 - Data Science Methods for Molecular Science and Engineering
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Covers fundamentals of machine learning and implementing data science in Python. Introduces modern data science methods taught in the context of molecular science and engineering spanning to the process scale. Connects theory to real-world applications in research or industry settings. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 545; A.

Course: CHEM 546 - Software Engineering for Molecular Science and Engineering
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduces basic principles of scientific software development in Python in the context of project-based work for molecular science and engineering spanning to the process scale. Covers command line tools, Python from the perspective of molecular and process engineering methods, software design, and development and collaboration principles (e.g., version control). Course overlaps with: CSE 583. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 546; W.

Course: CHEM 547 - Data Science Capstone Project
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: CHEM E 545/CHEM 545 and CHEM E 546/CHEM 546; recommended: prior exposure to data science fundamentals and software development. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 547; Sp.
Description: Involves teams of graduate students from molecular, materials or clean energy focused disciplines working on Data Science oriented research and engineering projects solicited from internal and external partners.  Employ modern team-based software engineering principles and cutting edge Data Science methods, including but not limited to machine learning, statistics, visualization and data management. Prerequisite: CHEM E 545/CHEM 545 and CHEM E 546/CHEM 546; recommended: prior exposure to data science fundamentals and software development. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 547; Sp.

Course: CHEM 550 - Quantum Mechanics of Atoms and Molecules
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Origins and basic postulates of quantum mechanics, solutions to single-particle problems, angular momentum and hydrogenic wave functions, matrix methods, perturbation theory, variational methods. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 551 - Quantum Dynamics and Spectroscopy
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: CHEM 550. Offered: W.
Description: Fundamental theory of spectroscopy and quantum dynamics; vibrational, electronic, X-ray and magnetic resonance spectroscopies; and application examples from current scientific literature. Prerequisite: CHEM 550. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 552 - Statistical Mechanics
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: CHEM 550. Offered: Sp.
Description: General theorems of statistical mechanics, relation of the equilibrium theory to classical thermodynamics, Legendre transformations, quantum statistics, theory of imperfect gases, lattice statistics, and theory of solids. Prerequisite: CHEM 550. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 553 - Advanced Statistical Mechanics
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: CHEM 552. Offered: Sp.
Description: Advanced topics in equilibrium and nonequilibrium statistical mechanics. Prerequisite: CHEM 552. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 558 - Spectroscopic Molecular Identification
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Basic theory of spectral techniques - infrared spectroscopy, NMR, and mass spectrometry - with emphasis on spectral interpretation skills needed for the elucidation of structure, conformation, and dynamics in organic and biological chemistry. Offered: A.

Course: CHEM 560 - Current Problems in Physical Chemistry
Credits: 1-3, max. 12
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Primarily for doctoral candidates in physical chemistry. A discussion of topics selected from active research fields. See department for instructor and the topic during any particular quarter.

Course: CHEM 561 - Introduction to Quantum Information Science and Engineering for Chemists and Materials Scientists
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: CHEM 455 or CHEM 475. Offered: jointly with MSE 561; A.
Description: Introduction to the core concepts of quantum information science and engineering including mathematical and quantum mechanical foundations, qubits, coherence, entanglement, applications, and materials systems Prerequisite: CHEM 455 or CHEM 475. Offered: jointly with MSE 561; A.

Course: CHEM 565 - Computational Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Basics of molecular quantum chemistry (Hartree-Fock and density functional theory); numerical implementation using computers, including basics of programming and scientific computing; applications to problems in chemistry; use of computational chemistry software packages to study chemical reactions and molecular properties. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 566 - Energy Materials, Devices, and Systems
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Provides project-based training for synthesis and characterization of new energy materials for generation and storage and integrating renewables into energy systems. Employs instruments at the Clean Energy Research Training Testbeds, a UW user facility. Topics include nanoparticle synthesis, solar cell and module characterization, coin cell battery assembly and testing, photochemistry, 2D semiconductors, and grid simulation. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 540/MSE 566/PHYS 566; A.

Course: CHEM 567 - Computers in Data Acquisition and Analysis
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Interface computers to  a variety of laboratory equipment such as Geiger Counter, pH titration,  spectrophotometer, PID controlled magnetic induction device, or an acoustic tube.  Students will individually interface the computer to the equipment, write the code to drive the experiment,  and analyze or model the data.  Utilizes LabView, Matlab,  Octave Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 571 - Current Research Topics in Inorganic Chemistry
Credits: 1, max. 18
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Focused discussion of ongoing research occurring across the department in the area of Inorganic Chemistry Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.

Course: CHEM 572 - Current Research Topics in Bioanalytical Chemistry
Credits: 1, max. 18
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Discussion of ongoing research in bioanalytical and analytical chemistry. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.

Course: CHEM 573 - Current Research Topics in Organic and Biological Chemistry
Credits: 1, max. 18
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Discussion of ongoing research occurring in organic chemistry and chemical biology. Offered: AWSp.

Course: CHEM 574 - Current Research Topics in Spectroscopy
Credits: 1, max. 18
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Ongoing research in the area of spectroscopy. Offered: AWSp.

Course: CHEM 575 - Current Research Topics in Theoretical and Computational Chemistry
Credits: 1, max. 18
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Focused discussion of ongoing research occurring across the department in the area of theoretical and computational chemistry. Offered: AWSp.

Course: CHEM 578 - Current Research Topics in Materials Chemistry
Credits: 1, max. 18
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Focused ongoing research in Materials Chemistry. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.

Course: CHEM 581 - Preparation for Second-Year Exam
Credits: 3-, max. 9
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Preparation for examination. Open only to students accepted for doctoral work in chemistry, in their second year of study. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.

Course: CHEM 584 - Electronic and Optoelectronic Polymers
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: either CHEM 453, CHEM 455, CHEM 475, or equivalent background. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 584; A.
Description: Covers the chemistry, physics, materials science, and applications of semiconducting and metallic conjugated polymers. Examines the structural origins of the diverse electronic and optoelectronic properties of conjugated polymers. Exemplifies applications by light-emitting diodes, lasers, solar cells, thin film transistors, electrochromic devices, biosensors, and batteries. Prerequisite: either CHEM 453, CHEM 455, CHEM 475, or equivalent background. Offered: jointly with CHEM E 584; A.

Course: CHEM 585 - Electronic Structure and Application of Materials
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduction to electronic structure theory of solids from a chemical perspective, including band theory and the free electron model, with an emphasis on modern trends in research in inorganic materials in the bulk and on the nanometer scale. Recommended: familiarity with particle in a box; free electron model; symmetry and symmetry elements; molecular orbital theory; principles of inorganic chemistry; and ability to independently research and learn advanced topics. Offered: W.

Course: CHEM 586 - Electronic Dynamics in Organic and Inorganic Materials
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Energy and charge transfer; exciton migration and charge transport; photophysical dynamics in optoelectronic and kinetic processes in electrochemical energy conversion. Recommended: working knowledge of electromagnetism; calculus; differential equations; and linear algebra. Offered: Sp.

Course: CHEM 587 - Nanomaterials Chemistry and Engineering
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: CHEM 455; MATH 207; and CHEM E 326; recommended: classical physics, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, and ordinary and partial differential equations Offered: jointly with CHEM E 535; Sp.
Description: Rigorous overview of fundamental chemical and physical concepts important to nanomaterials science and engineering. Focus on luminescent, plasmonic, magnetic nanomaterials. Students will learn basic concepts prevalent in the nanomaterials literature, and develop rigorous mathematical understanding of fundamental principles that govern many of the advanced materials that are currently under development in the field. Prerequisite: CHEM 455; MATH 207; and CHEM E 326; recommended: classical physics, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, and ordinary and partial differential equations Offered: jointly with CHEM E 535; Sp.

Credits: 1, max. 18

Description: For chemistry graduate students only. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.

Description: For chemistry graduate students only. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.

Course: CHEM 593 - Seminar in Organic Chemistry

Description: For chemistry graduate students only. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.

Description: Weekly seminars on current topics in molecular Engineering. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: jointly with MOLENG 520; AWSp.
