Description: Weekly group conferences concerning ongoing graduate student and postdoctoral research in immunology. Students may register for more than one conference each quarter. Prerequisite: graduate standing in immunology. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: TECHIN 513 - Managing Data and Signal Processing
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Students will gain the understanding needed to process low level sensor data, analyze and interpret that data using basic machine learning and signal processing, and then store the data in the cloud for later retrieval. Offered: W.

Course: B A 495 - Business Internship
Credits: 1-4, max. 8
General Education: 
Prerequisites: ACCTG 225. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSpS.
Description: Internship with a private firm, nonprofit organization, or government agency, where work experience involves substantial application of business concepts learned in the classroom. Prerequisite: ACCTG 225. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: FAMED 683 - P-Clinical Clerkship in Family Medicine - Lewiston
Credits: 12
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: For description and prerequisite, see FAMED 632. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: EDLPS 524 - Seminar in Philosophy of Education
Credits: 3, max. 6
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Philosophical examination of ways in which education might be studied. Uses and limits of conventional scientific approaches in education inquiry. Consideration of alternatives.

Course: GEOG 258 - Digital Geographies
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Explores the use and societal impacts of contemporary digital spatial technologies. Focuses on internet mapping, handheld geographic technologies, location-based services, spatial applications of social media, the geoweb, and traditional GIS. Develops hands-on experience using online digital spatial tools for geovisual representation, and skills for evaluation/critique of digital data and maps.

Course: MUSIC 421 - Organ Improvisation and Service Playing II
Credits: 2
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: MUSIC 420. Offered: W.
Description: Continuation of MUSIC 420. Includes brief review of figured bass and functional harmony, free improvisation in simple antecedent/consequent ABA forms and more complex forms (rondo, theme, and variation), improvising partitas, interludes, improvisations based on plainchant. A survey of important improvisation texts. Prerequisite: MUSIC 420. Offered: W.

Course: GEN ST 161 - Discovery Seminar in Individuals and Society
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Small intensive seminar focusing on individuals and society taught during Early Fall Start led by faculty representing a wide spectrum of academic disciplines and interests. Offered: A.

Course: BIBHEB 399 - Study Abroad
Credits: 1-15, max. 15
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Credit for intermediate Hebrew in an approved Study Abroad program. Requires credit evaluation by department or faculty. Does not automatically apply to major or minor requirements. Course overlaps with: MODHEB 399.

Course: BIOST 552 - Statistical Genetics III: Design and Analysis
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: STAT/BIOST 551; GENOME 371; or permission of instructor. Offered: jointly with STAT 552; W.
Description: Overview of probability models, inheritance models, penetrance. Association and linkage. The lod score method. Affected sib method. Fitting complex inheritance models. Design mapping studies; multipoint, disequilibrium, and fine-scale mapping. Ascertainment. Prerequisite: STAT/BIOST 551; GENOME 371; or permission of instructor. Offered: jointly with STAT 552; W.

Course: MARBIO 460 - Aquatic Animals Research Experience
Credits: 6
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: A hands-on introduction of "doing science" in close collaboration with a faculty member. Students engage in research around a thematic focus of aquatic animals, with lab experiments and field work. Students gather, analyze, write up, and present their own data. Offered: jointly with FHL 460; ASp.

Course: ESS 502 - The Solid Earth
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Concepts of internal earth processes: Earth as heat engine and chemical processor, style of mantle convection, origin and evolution of the Earth's magnetic field, Cascadia subduction and hazards. Introduces seismology, fluid dynamics, heat flow, gravity, and geomagnetism. Focuses on the analysis, critique, and communication of ideas from scientific literature.

Course: MUSIC 325 - Music in Cinema
Credits: 5
General Education: A&H/SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Surveys representative film soundtracks from the past one hundred years. Examines the role of music and sound design within cinematic narrative form; explores theories of film music; and lays the groundwork for engaging film as a multimedia art form. Offered: S.

Course: ENV H 306 - Health and Sustainability
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc/SSc, DIV
Prerequisites: None
Description: Focuses on the intersection of human health and environmental sustainability. Introduces core concepts of sustainability and public health, and explores the intersections of health and sustainability in specific domains including energy, transportation, the built environment, food systems, and chemicals. Emphasizes a systems thinking approach to formulating solutions. Offered: A.

Course: NEURO 561 - From Biophysics to Neural Computation
Credits: 2
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduces the mathematics and methods of neuronal modeling. Develops, compares, and relates dynamical systems approaches and empirical characterizations of neuronal function. Includes lectures, student-led journal paper discussions, biweekly computational workshops on neuronal modeling packages, and a computations project. Offered: jointly with P BIO 561; Sp.

Course: DENTPC 577 - Periodontics 2: Prevention/Periodontics
Credits: 2
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduction to prevention in dentistry. Topics covered include examination of the dentition and periodontium, dental disease indices, scaling and root planning instruments and instrumentation, sharpening, and oral hygiene chemotherapeutics. Students prepare for providing patient care in the next course, DENTPC 587-Periodontics 3. Offered: W.

Course: NEURO 510 - Seminar in Neuroscience
Credits: 0.5, max. 30
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Seminar of advanced in-depth coverage on neuroscience topics, current interests, and the latest research that is being conducted. Lectures by program faculty and invited speakers. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.

Course: B ECON 527 - International Finance
Credits: 4
General Education: 
Prerequisites: MBA core finance.
Description: Study of selected problems in financing, international trade, investment, and foreign business operations; international aspects of money markets; problems of evaluation of foreign investments. Prerequisite: MBA core finance.

Course: SPHSC 600 - Independent Study or Research
Credits: *-
General Education: 
Prerequisites: permission of instructor. Offered: AWSpS.
Description: Prerequisite: permission of instructor. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: JSIS E 478 - Readings in the Social Sciences in Japanese
Credits: 3-5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: JAPAN 313.
Description: Introduction to articles and short works in economics, history, political science, and other social sciences. Assignments chosen from major Japanese monthlies and academic works. All readings in Japanese. Prerequisite: JAPAN 313.

Course: GWSS 556 - Decolonial Feminist Theory and Practice
Credits: 5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Examines relationships among colonialism, imperialism, and occupation and racial, gender, and sexual hierarchies. Students focus on successful struggles for justice, freedom, and sovereignty. Develops skills to understand approaches to research and the politics of knowledge production.

Course: MSE 197 - Case Studies in Materials Innovation
Credits: 2
General Education: 
Prerequisites: either CHEM 142, CHEM 143, or CHEM 145. Offered: Sp.
Description: Materials science concepts, with emphasis on career opportunities in Materials Science and Engineering. Includes structural materials, electronic materials, biomaterials, and energy related materials. Development of scientific analysis and research proposal formulation skills. Prerequisite: either CHEM 142, CHEM 143, or CHEM 145. Offered: Sp.

Course: E E 547 - Linear Systems Theory
Credits: 4
General Education: 
Prerequisites: E E 510/A A 510/CHEM E 510/M E 510. Offered: jointly with A A 547.
Description: Linearity, linearization, finite dimensionality, time-varying vs. time-invariant linear systems, interconnection of linear systems, functional/structural descriptions of linear systems, system zeros and invertibility, linear system stability, system norms, state transition, matrix exponentials, controllability and observability, realization theory. Course overlaps with: EE P 547; M E 547; TECE 551; and TECE 555. Prerequisite: E E 510/A A 510/CHEM E 510/M E 510. Offered: jointly with A A 547.

Course: COM 351 - Interviewing Principles and Practices
Credits: 5
General Education: A&H/SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Interviewing principles and practices, with emphasis on information gathering, selection, and persuasive interviews. Purposes and types of interviews, structure of interviews, and influence of communication patterns on interview outcomes.

Course: EPI 515 - Advanced Epidemiologic Methods I
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: EPI 512 and EPI 513 Offered: jointly with BIOST 519.
Description: First in a series of 2 courses. Increases knowledge of epidemiological principles by introducing methodological approaches to handling common problems in epidemiologic research that extend beyond the scope of traditional methods. Prerequisite: EPI 512 and EPI 513 Offered: jointly with BIOST 519.

Course: ASIAN 404 - Writing Systems
Credits: 5
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Comprehensive theoretical and historical overview of written language worldwide. Includes origins and early development of writing in the Near East, Asia, and the Americas; relationships between spoken and written languages; types and characteristic of writing systems (logographics, syllabic, and alphabetic); and methods used for decipherment of ancient languages. Offered: W.

Course: DANCE 490 - Special Studies in Dance
Credits: 1-5, max. 20
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Special studies designed to address contemporary and historical concerns in the field of dance.

Course: GERMAN 341 - Franz Kafka in English
Credits: 5
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Short stories and novels of Franz Kafka; emphasis on philosophical relevance and esthetic significance.

Course: B H 513 - P-Ethical Responsibilities of Medical Practice
Credits: 2
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Provides intensive and practical guidance about management of principal ethical and legal problems that arise in clinical practice: informed consent, confidentiality, decisions regarding life-support, advance directives and surrogate decision-makers, duty to care for indigent and risky patients. One week intensive course. Offered: S.

Course: HSTCMP 200 - Ten Events That Shook the World
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Offers introduction to history by examining ten events of great importance for both past and present. The ten events, which vary from quarter to quarter, come from diverse times and places, thereby encouraging a sweeping view of world history. (See department advisor for the current quarterly list of the ten events.)

Course: SOC W 569 - Community-Centered Integrative Practice
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: This interactive student-centered course shifts the paradigm from the binary of macro vs micro and elevates the importance of relationships, connectivity, and allyship as acts of love, justice and resistance. Provides advanced skill building in assessing and maximizing community strengths, empowering practices and coalition building.

Course: OTOHN 675 - P-Otolaryngology Clerkship Bozeman, MT
Credits: 4-8, max. 8
General Education: 
Prerequisites: third or fourth year medical student; recommended: patient-care courses in internal medicine or surgery. Offered: AWSpS.
Description: Surgical subspecialty of otolaryngology-head and neck surgery is structured to allow broad introduction to breadth of specialty. Students see patients in clinic, join inpatient rounds, and have an opportunity to go to the operating room. Prerequisite: third or fourth year medical student; recommended: patient-care courses in internal medicine or surgery. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: DENTCL 650 - Biomedical Foundations for Clinical Dentistry
Credits: 1-, max. 2
General Education: 
Prerequisites: third-year predoctoral student in UW School of Dentistry. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: WSp.
Description: Reviews biomedical foundations and integrates knowledge with clinical dental practice. Uses practice Integrated National Board Dental Exam (INBDE) questions and supplementary study materials to self-assess knowledge integration. Students take mock INBDE exams, including a baseline pre-test. Prerequisite: third-year predoctoral student in UW School of Dentistry. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: WSp.

Course: BIOEN 594 - Advanced Drug Delivery
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Provides students with an understanding of the current state of the art for advanced drug delivery. Covers the major families of biologic drugs, major challenges associated with their delivery and specific disease applications. Offered: Sp.

Course: KOREAN 445 - Foreign Study: Korean Literature
Credits: 1-15, max. 20
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Modern 400-level Korean language studied abroad in approved programs in Korean. Evaluation by department/faculty required.

Course: IPM 510 - Water Systems
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Water and water supply as a system element. Water and especially freshwater, as an essential and limited resource. Looks at aging water infrastructure; user conflicts; changes in water distribution tied to climate changes; intergovernmental policy, programs, and relationship; management strategies and tools; and their effect on water and water supply. Offered: jointly with URBAN 584; AW.

Course: R E 510 - Introduction to Real Estate
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Provides a basic overview of the participants, processes, workings of different components of the real estate industry (including a variety of uses spanning from residential, office, retail and industrial to specialized) as well as the quantitative components of the real estate decision-making. Additionally, students are introduced to an overview of construction management, sustainability, corporate services, property law and ethics. Offered: jointly with URBAN 552; AW.

Course: BIOEN 586 - Tissue Engineering
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Tissue structure and function, scaffold design, applications to specialized tissues and organs. Offered: W.

Course: EDSPE 504 - Special Education and the Law
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Overview of major state and federal laws affecting the operation and management of special education programs in public schools. Emphasis upon procedural and substantive rights of children with disabling conditions. Course overlaps with: T EDSP 547. Offered: jointly with EDLPS 516.

Course: ATMOS 370 - Atmospheric Structure and Analysis
Credits: 5
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: ATMOS 301. Offered: W.
Description: Structure and evolution of extratropical cyclones, fronts, and convective systems. Surface and upper air analysis techniques. Radar and satellite data. Real-world applications of basic dynamical principles. Introduction to operational products and forecasting. Prerequisite: ATMOS 301. Offered: W.

Course: PRSAN 543 - Modern Persian Literature: A Survey
Credits: 5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: PRSAN 523.
Description: Development of poetry and prose after Iran felt and absorbed the impact of Western cultures. Periods and genres. Works of such authors as Jamalzadeh, Hedayat, Dehkoda, Al-e Ahmad, Nima, Sepehri, and Forugh. Prerequisite: PRSAN 523.

Course: SEFS 526 - Seminar in Advanced Silviculture
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: ESRM 428. Offered: W.
Description: Seminar on current and emerging silvicultural issues and underlying biological principles. Topics include: stand management to enhance wildlife, biodiversity, and high productivity in sub-tropical and tropical regions; computer simulation of stand growth; adaptation to changes in management objectives; soil conditions and productivity during stand rotation; and minimizing effects of catastrophic disruption. Prerequisite: ESRM 428. Offered: W.

Course: ANTH 213 - Anthropology and Sport
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc, DIV
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduces theories, methods, and findings of sociocultural anthropology through a focus on sport. Considers sport as linked to identities, nationalism, gender, race, class, religion, and other issues. Explores cultural rituals of sport, potentials and obstacles to sport transcending social differences, and sport's role in education, youth development, and community building.

Course: OTOHN 499 - Undergraduate Research
Credits: *, max. 35
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Research opportunities offered under direction in the area of otolaryngology. (Twelve weeks.) Offered: AWSpS.

Course: NMETH 533 - Appraisal and Translation of Evidence for Practice
Credits: 5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: either NMETH 535 or permission of instructor.
Description: Designed to enhance use of methods to critically appraise literature, design, and implement processes to evaluate outcomes of practice, and promote patient-centered care. Applies relevant findings to improve practice, develop guidelines, and use information technology and research methods. Includes dissemination of findings. Prerequisite: either NMETH 535 or permission of instructor.

Course: DRAMA 202 - Creative Leadership: A Course in Courage
Credits: 5
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Courage as the ability to move through fear rather than becoming paralyzed by it. Examines sources of fear and obstacles that keep us from becoming our fullest, most human, most successful selves. Aimed at developing, demonstrating, and exercising both courage and leadership's other critical skills: connecting and communicating.

Course: PEDS 562 - Ethical Issues in Pediatrics
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Provides a survey of contemporary ethical issues that arise in the clinical and research environment when children are involved, including the role of children and adolescents in decision-making, the limits of parental decision-making authority, and issues related to genetic testing, transplantation, research, and public health. Offered: jointly with B H 562; A.

Course: ESS 436 - Planetary Physics and Chemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: MATH 125; and either PHYS 114 and PHYS 117, PHYS 121, or PHYS 141; recommended: familiarity with single variable differentiation and integration.
Description: Provides introduction to the physics and chemistry that govern planetary interiors, surfaces, atmospheres, and dynamics. Topics include: planetary surface processes such as cratering and volcanism; planetary interiors, heat flow, and tectonics; gravity, dynamics, and tides; planetary atmospheres, radiative transfer, and climate; meteorites and cosmochemistry; and the origin of planetary systems. Prerequisite: MATH 125; and either PHYS 114 and PHYS 117, PHYS 121, or PHYS 141; recommended: familiarity with single variable differentiation and integration.

Course: ENV H 526 - Leadership in Public Health I
Credits: 1
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Designed for students who are serving on the School of Public Health Dean's Advisory Council of Students (DACS). Focuses on development of personal leadership skills and acumen. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: A.

Course: MUSIC 457 - Jazz Laboratory: Theory and Application of Rhythm
Credits: 1
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Establishes a fundamental comprehension of the complex and nuanced rhythmic structures inherent in traditional and modern jazz. Through transcription, analysis, dictation, composition and performance. Students develop a personal understanding of, and the ability to execute, the detailed rhythmic language that defines this art form. Offered: A.

Course: HSERV 517 - Qualitative Research Methods for Health Systems and Population Health
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Builds on introductory training in qualitative research methods by diving deeper into different frameworks, study designs, sampling approaches, and data collections tools. Covers various data analytic approaches, as well as data visualization, interpretation, writing and presenting qualitative research findings. Students learn to apply these concepts and execute a qualitative research project from start to finish. Course overlaps with: NMETH 535 and NMETH 588.

Course: FAMED 645 - P-Clinical Clerkship in Family Medicine - Kaiser Permanente Seattle
Credits: 1-24, max. 25
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: For description and prerequisite, see FAMED 632. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: SOC 469 - Balkan Societies
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Examination of the roots of Balkan social problems (economic backwardness, minority-group conflicts, peasant problem), the failure of pre-1945 attempts to solve these problems, the post-1945 communist failures, the causes of the upheavals of 1989, and the prospects for success in the 1990s.

Course: DXARTS 480 - Introduction to Data Driven Arts
Credits: 5
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: In contemporary digital culture, diverse media can be understood as data - from text and images, to recorded sound and speech. Introduces tools for collecting, processing, and organizing archives of multimedia. Establishes a foundation for artistic experimentation with machine learning and artificial intelligence systems. Involves working creatively with data from text and images, recorded sound and speech. Offered: A.

Course: PHIL 470 - Intermediate Logic
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc/NSc, RSN
Prerequisites: None
Description: An introduction to the concepts and methods of metatheory and their application to the sentential calculus.

Course: ENDO 658 - Endodontic Emergency Rotation
Credits: 1
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Clinical experience in managing and treating patients in pain. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: HSTAM 335 - The Age of Nero
Credits: 5
General Education: A&H/SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Detailed study of the history and culture of the reign of the Roman Emperor Nero (AD 54-68).  Includes readings in the historian Tacitus' account of Nero, as well as in authors such as Petronius, Lucan, and Seneca, and consideration of the artistic and architectural achievements of the period. Recommended: HSTAM 111, HSTAM 302, HSTAM 312, or HSTAM 313; CLAS 122, CLAS 320, CLAS 329, or CLAS 330 Offered: jointly with CLAS 335; AWSpS.

Course: ECFS 456 - Senior Project III
Credits: 2
General Education: 
Prerequisites: ECFS 410; ECFS 411; ECFS 454; and ECFS 455.
Description: Third of a three-quarter sequence leading to the completion and presentation of the senior project during the final quarter in the major. Provides advanced opportunities to integrate theory and practice in community-based learning and research experience continues during the quarter. Prerequisite: ECFS 410; ECFS 411; ECFS 454; and ECFS 455.

Course: AAS 403 - Survey of Asian American Poetry
Credits: 5
General Education: A&H, DIV
Prerequisites: None
Description: Asian American poetry, nineteenth century to present. Readings include poetry of the early immigrant to America, cultural imperatives transferred from old world to new world, and establishment of an Asian American identity in poetry from 1870s through 1890s.

Course: HEOR 340 - Introduction to Health Economics
Credits: 3
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Applies core microeconomic concepts to the study of health care markets and the U.S. health systems. Students use economic models and analytic tools to explore a wide range of topics such as health insurance design, provider incentives, pharmaceutical markets, and current health policy debates. Recommended: ECON 200. Offered: jointly with ECON 344/PHRMSC 330; A.

Course: NMETH 210 - Science, Evidence and Health: Mastering Health Information and Personal Health Technologies
Credits: 4/5
General Education: SSc/NSc, DIV
Prerequisites: None
Description: Provides foundations for becoming skilled consumers of health information and health technologies.  Using current topics in health, students will learn to navigate the available health information, understand its quality, become familiar with personal health technologies, and link information learned to their health and the health of their communities. Offered: W.

Course: MUSIC 379 - Junior Recital
Credits: 1
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: For participants in the Bachelor of Music degree program only.

Course: HCDE 210 - Explorations in Human Centered Design
Credits: 3
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Explores the core principles, methodologies, and applications of human centered design practice. Areas of investigation include user research, ideation, interaction design, visualization, prototyping, and usability. Cannot be taken for credit if credit has already been earned for HCDE 302.

Course: G H 541 - Fundamentals of Implementation Science in Global Health
Credits: 4/5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Provides an introduction to the emerging field of implementation research by outlining various methods that are applied to improving implementation (including applied engineering, management tools, health systems, and policy research), and using experiential case studies from global health leaders. Addresses barriers to effective replication and scale-up in local settings. Offered: jointly with HMS 541; Sp.

Course: HSTAA 212 - The Military History of the United States From Colonial Times to the Present
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Development of American military policies, organizational patterns, tactics, and weaponry, from beginnings as a seventeenth-century frontier defense force to the global conflicts and military commitments of the twentieth century. Interaction and tension between need for an effective military force and concept of civilian control of that force. Course equivalent to: T HIST 212.

Course: IND E 519 - Healthcare Modeling and Decision Making
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Applications of operations research in healthcare. Introduction to a variety of modeling techniques including decision analysis, cost-effectiveness analysis, Markov models, Markov decision processes, dynamic programming, simulation, queuing, scheduling, machine learning and their applications in healthcare management and medical decision making.

Course: DANCE 125 - Beginning Tap
Credits: 2/3, max. 12
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduction to tap technique. Offered: AWSp.

Course: BIOC 442 - Biochemistry
Credits: 4
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either 2.2 in BIOC 406 or 2.2 in BIOC 441, or a 2.2 in BIOC 451. Offered: Sp.
Description: Biochemistry and molecular biology for undergraduate students in molecular and cellular biology, for biochemistry majors, and graduate students in other science departments. Prerequisite: either 2.2 in BIOC 406 or 2.2 in BIOC 441, or a 2.2 in BIOC 451. Offered: Sp.

Course: POL S 352 - American Political Parties
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Theories of American parties, campaigns, and voting behavior; party leadership; political socialization and participation.

Course: FAMED 535 - Medical Chinese Terminology
Credits: 1
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: For healthcare professions students interested in expanding cultural understanding and improving communication with patients whose primary language is Mandarin Chinese. Includes common Mandarin Chinese medical terminology used during medical visits; Chinese culture and beliefs toward health and sickness; and cross cultural comparison of healthcare delivery in China and the United States. Recommended: Some conversational level Chinese will be helpful and basic training in medical history taking. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: Sp.

Course: LAW B 544 - Space Law and Policy
Credits: 4
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Law and policy foundations of outer space activities. Essential origins, sources, and role of space law, as well as key institutions, forums, and forces shaping the contemporary governance of space activities. Provides a thorough grounding in U.N. treaties, principles, resolutions, regulations, and private international and national space laws and policies. Offered: Sp.

Course: JSIS A 354 - Narcoculture: Propaganda and Publicity in the War on Drugs
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Representation of so-called narcos in inter-American media and culture since the 1970s. Students critically analyze U.S. films, Colombian soap operas, Mexican ballads, and state propaganda dedicated to portraying traffickers' exploits. Centering on the ethical question of how to portray drug-related violence, introduces students to debates about censorship, propaganda, the public sphere, and spectacle.

Course: CM 512 - Preconstruction Facilitation
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Studies the preconstruction phase of a building construction project by facilitating the work of a multi-disciplinary team focusing on developing the conceptual design for a construction project.

Course: G H 554 - Bioengineering Solutions to Improve the Health of Families Worldwide
Credits: 1
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Interdisciplinary discussions about global health.  Explores how bioengineering approaches contribute to the study of problems of global health importance, the development of diagnostics, and the discovery of interventional strategies to improve human health. Emphasizes collaboration between students and researchers with backgrounds in infectious disease, basic science, and bioengineering. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: jointly with BIOEN 554; A.

Course: HSTCMP 270 - Race, Religion, and Migration in Global Context
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc, DIV
Prerequisites: None
Description: Migration of "Middle Easterners" - Jews, Christians, and Muslims - from the Ottoman Empire to the United States in the twentieth century.  How their experiences shaped, and were shaped by, the development of racial categories, definitions of citizenship and national belonging, and broader political, religious, and cultural dynamics linking the Mediterranean world to the Americas. Offered: jointly with JEW ST 270.

Course: ESS 510 - Advanced Applied Geology Field Investigations
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: ESS 509; three of ESS 420, ESS 454, ESS 526, ESS 527, or ESS 547; recommended: undergraduate degree in geology or closely related field; and an undergraduate field course related to geology. Offered: Sp.
Description: Application of applied geology core curriculum to field problems. Includes multi-day intensive, field trips in the Pacific Northwest to study the intersection of society and the environment and to gain working knowledge of the geology there.  Focus on field techniques, designing an investigation, recording observations, and report writing Prerequisite: ESS 509; three of ESS 420, ESS 454, ESS 526, ESS 527, or ESS 547; recommended: undergraduate degree in geology or closely related field; and an undergraduate field course related to geology. Offered: Sp.

Course: PABIO 700 - Master's Thesis
Credits: *-
General Education: 
Prerequisites: permission of Graduate Program Adviser. Credit/no-credit only.
Description: Prerequisite: permission of Graduate Program Adviser. Credit/no-credit only.

Course: ATMOS 503 - Atmospheric Motions I
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Basic equations governing atmospheric motions and their elementary applications; circulation and vorticity; dynamics of midlatitude disturbances. Offered: A.

Course: AES 335 - History of African Americans and Sports
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc, DIV
Prerequisites: None
Description: Development of sport in the US and its importance for US culture and society. Covers increased centrality of athletic competition as part of the new leisure time in the late - 19th century, revival of the Olympic movement, racial segregation/integration, today's American notions of celebrity and social style.

Course: G H 501 - Core Topics in Global Health
Credits: 1
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Examines a variety of foundational global health topics including maternal, adolescent, and child health; nutrition; infectious diseases; environmental health; non-communicable diseases; and mental health. Within each topic area, we will define the problems, complexities, and context, and establish the need for multidisciplinary approaches. Offered: A.

Course: SWED 399 - Foreign Study: Topics in Swedish Literature and Culture
Credits: 1-5, max. 15
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Topics in Swedish literature, life, and civilization.

Course: E E 453 - Electric Drives
Credits: 5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: a minimum grade of 1.0 in E E 452; and a minimum grade of 1.0 in  E E 458.
Description: Elements of drive systems, speed-torque characteristics of electric motors and industrial loads, solid-state converter. Starting and braking methods of loaded motors. Speed control of electric motors. Solid-state drives. Transient analysis of loaded motors. Special forms of individual- and multimotor drives. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 1.0 in E E 452; and a minimum grade of 1.0 in  E E 458.

Course: ANTH 523 - Seminar on Religious and Political Violence
Credits: 5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Employs ethnographic studies and anthropological theory to examine the relationships between culture and power in the analysis of religious and political violence. Topics include modernity; secularisms and fundamentalisms; ritual, sacrifice, and martyrdom; law, rights, and subject-making. Offered: jointly with JSIS B 523.

Course: DXARTS 491 - Senior Thesis I
Credits: 5-
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introductory course of the senior thesis sequence. Includes weekly seminars, selection of a thesis topic, and contract with an appropriate faculty adviser. Majors and senior standing only. Offered: A.

Course: GWSS 257 - Psychology of Gender
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc, DIV
Prerequisites: None
Description: Major psychological theories of gender-role development; biological and environmental influences that determine and maintain gender differences in behavior; roles in children and adults; topics include aggression, cognitive abilities, achievement motivation, affiliation. Course overlaps with: TPSYCH 400. Offered: jointly with PSYCH 257.

Course: POL S 569 - Law and Rights in Authoritative Regimes
Credits: 5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Explores role of law and courts and the nature of rights in authoritarian regimes. Questions addressed include why authoritarian regimes promote "rule-of-law", who is empowered by law, and the political consequences of "rule-of-law promotion. Offered: jointly with JSIS B 569.

Course: MICROM 445 - Medical Virology
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: either BIOL 180 or BIOL 200.
Description: Introduces medical virology emphasizing basic understanding of the pathogenesis and replication of medically important viruses including the spread, diagnosis, epidemiology, treatment, and prevention of human viral diseases. Prerequisite: either BIOL 180 or BIOL 200.

Course: JAPAN 361 - Topics in Japanese Cinema and Media
Credits: 5, max. 15
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduces Japanese film through topics organized according to a specific theme or focused on a relatively limited time period. Students learn contemporary approaches to film with an emphasis on understanding them within their social and historical contexts, often through a specific interpretive methodology.

Course: MICROM 599 - Research Presentations
Credits: 2
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Current research review. Credit/no-credit only.

Course: OCEAN 590 - Advanced Topics in Oceanography
Credits: 9-18, max. 18
General Education: 
Prerequisites: permission of Director of Friday Harbor Laboratories. Offered: S.
Description: Advanced topics examining specialized and interdisciplinary areas of oceanographic research. Offered at Friday Harbor Laboratories. Prerequisite: permission of Director of Friday Harbor Laboratories. Offered: S.

Course: C LIT 250 - Introduction to Comparative Literature: Literature and Culture
Credits: 5, max. 15
General Education: A&H/SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Study of literature in its relation to culture. Focuses on literature as a cultural institution, directly related to the construction of individual identity and the dissemination and critique of values.

Course: CLAS 445 - Greek and Roman Religion
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc/A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Religion in the social life of the Greeks and Romans, with emphasis placed on their public rituals and festivals. Attention is given to the priesthoods, personal piety, rituals of purification and healing, and the conflict of religions in the early Roman Empire. Many lectures illustrated by slides. Offered: jointly with RELIG 445.

Course: PHRMRA 536 - Skills for the Regulatory Affairs Professional
Credits: 2
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Covers essential skills in regulatory affairs and includes an overview of local medical products companies. Offered: A.

Course: E E 242 - Signals, Systems, and Data I
Credits: 5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: either MATH 135,  MATH 207, or AMATH 351, any of which may be taken concurrently; and either E E 241 or CSE 163. Offered: AWSp.
Description: Introduction to signal processing, including both continuous- and discrete-time signals and systems. Basic signals including impulses, unit steps, periodic signals and complex exponentials. Convolution of signals. Fourier series and transforms. Linear, time-invariant filters. Computer laboratory. Course overlaps with: E E 235; B EE 235; B EE 341; and TCES 310. Prerequisite: either MATH 135,  MATH 207, or AMATH 351, any of which may be taken concurrently; and either E E 241 or CSE 163. Offered: AWSp.

Course: ASTBIO 115 - Astrobiology: Life in the Universe
Credits: 5
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduction to the new science of astrobiology, study of the origin and evolution of life on Earth, and the search for microbial and intelligent life elsewhere in the universe. Designed for non-science majors.

Course: G H 502 - Current Research and Programs in Global Health
Credits: 1
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Examines current research and programs in Global Health priority areas with an emphasis on the use of research evidence to inform policy and implementation strategies in programmatic settings. Evidence-based approaches to address key global health issues in maternal, adolescent, and child health, infectious diseases, environmental health, and non-communicable diseases will be evaluated. Offered: W.

Course: ATMOS 586 - Current Research in Climate Change
Credits: 2, max. 20
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Weekly lectures focusing on a particular aspect of climate (topic to change each year) from invited speakers (both UW and outside), plus one or two keynote speakers, followed by class discussion. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: jointly with ESS 586/OCEAN 586.

Course: HIHIM 520 - Law, Policy, and Ethics in Health Information
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Explores the laws, policies, and issues involved in oversight and management of health data and health information systems. Defines the legal health record and the requirements, role, and uses. Covers the legal and ethical framework, issues and concepts, and the role of e-discovery on the emerging health data environment. Offered: W.

Course: ITAL 127 - Beginning Conversational Italian
Credits: 2, max. 6
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Development of beginning-level Italian conversational skills through class discussions and oral presentations. Topics vary. Not open to native speakers.

Course: ITAL 466 - Italian Society in Cinema and Literature in Italian
Credits: 5, max. 15
General Education: A&H/SSc
Prerequisites: ITAL 302.
Description: Studies the evolution of Italian postwar society through the analysis of film and literature as well as critical, historical, and sociological readings. Offered in Italian. Prerequisite: ITAL 302.

Course: PATH 509 - Fundamentals of Medical Science
Credits: 7
General Education: 
Prerequisites: enrollment in the Master of Science in Anatomic Pathology program. Offered: S.
Description: Comprehensive introduction and review of fundamental concepts in basic science and medicine. Topics include molecular and cell biology, human physiology, genetics, biochemistry, and introductory pathology and histology concepts. Prerequisite: enrollment in the Master of Science in Anatomic Pathology program. Offered: S.

Course: A A 580 - Geometric Methods for Non-Linear Control Systems
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Analysis and design of nonlinear control systems focusing on differential geometric methods. Topics include controllability, observability, feedback linearization, invariant distributions, and local coordinate transformations. Emphasis on systems evolving on Lie groups and linearly uncontrollable systems. Offered: jointly with E E 580/M E 580; Sp, even years.

Course: ESRM 423 - International Trade, Marketing, and the Environment
Credits: 3
General Education: SSc/NSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduction to international trade, marketing, and environmental business. Concepts include plan writing, exporting and importing, carbon credits, green marketing, and how global exchange rates affect environmental assets such as forests. Offered: W.

Course: HSTCMP 590 - Topics in History
Credits: 5, max. 15
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Seminar on selected topics in general history, with special emphasis on preparation for field examinations. Topics vary according to interests of students and instructor.

Course: MUSIC 424 - Improvisation for Classical Musicians
Credits: 1, max. 12
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Improvisation techniques for the classical music performer, emphasizing creative expression and spontaneous composition. Recommended: any 300-level or 400-level MUSICP course. Offered: AWSp.

Course: FISH 563 - Ecosystem Based Fisheries Management Laboratory
Credits: 2
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Laboratory covering the theory and practice of ecosystem based fisheries management. Areas of emphasis includes by-catch avoidance, the interaction between physical and biotic habitat and fish productivity, trophic ecosystem models, area based management and dynamics of fishing fleets. Recommended: either Fish 454, Fish 458, or Fish 558; R programming experience. Offered: Sp, odd years.

Course: LAW A 562 - Employment Law
Credits: 3-5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Topical study of the employment relationship: its formation, duration, and termination. Topics include contracting for individual job security; unjust discharge; public policy protections; employee mobility; employee voice; privacy; wages and hours; unemployment; and health and safety. Focuses on the non-unionized private sector. Offered: AS.

Course: DENTCP 647 - Restorative Dentistry Topics - AN
Credits: 1
General Education: 
Prerequisites: all preclinical coursework and DENTCL 620. Offered: A.
Description: Students examine restorative and prosthodontic principles essential to general dental practice. Emphasis placed on evidence-based treatment planning, diagnostic reasoning, and clinical decision-making through case-based learning and literature review. Prerequisite: all preclinical coursework and DENTCL 620. Offered: A.

Course: JSIS B 358 - International Cybercrime
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Addresses the issue of cybercrime as an international and political phenomenon. Discusses hackers and hacking culture, hacktivists, types of cybercrime, cybercrime networks, the relationship between cybercrime and governments, what makes a country vulnerable to cybercrime, and the impact of cybercrime on geopolitics. Course overlaps with: CSS 315.

Course: ESS 508 - Great Geological Issues
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: graduate standing in earth sciences, or in history of science, or permission of instructor.
Description: History and development of geological and paleontological theories and controversies; philosophy and methodology that have driven scientific inquiry in the earth sciences. Requires a term paper analyzing primary material. Prerequisite: graduate standing in earth sciences, or in history of science, or permission of instructor.

Course: EPI 505 - Preventing Healthcare Associated Infections
Credits: 1
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Multidisciplinary approach to understanding, measuring, and developing policy to prevent healthcare associated infections. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: jointly with MED 540.

Course: PHARMP 521 - Foundations of Interprofessional Practice I
Credits: [0-1]-, max. 1
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Team-based training and experiential immersion in healthcare team functioning for PY2 pharmacy students. work with medical, nursing, physician assistant, social work, dental and dietetics students in patient care situations to apply evidence-based practice and quality improvement principles. Focuses on development of intra- and inter-professional roles and professional identity. Credit/no-credit only.

Course: PBSCI 525 - P-Psychiatry and the Law
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Explores issues at the interface of law and psychiatry through didactic curriculum and research. Trainees develop an individualized research project with the assistance of their faculty mentors. Covers topics in civil and criminal forensic psychiatry, research ethics, research design, grantsmanship, and mental health law. Offered: Sp.

Course: JSIS A 430 - The Soviet Empire: Creation, Consolidation, and Collapse
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Surveys history of Soviet military and Soviet empire from 1917 to 1985, breakup of the USSR during 1985 to 1991, and the emergence of new security issues among those Eurasian states that formally constituted the national components of the USSR and its communist military allies.

Course: NURS 422 - Advanced Clinical Judgement
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: NURS 401; NURS 405; and NCLIN 407.
Description: Provides opportunity to advance clinical judgment skills of individual patients and groups of patients in preparation for practice. Focuses on prioritizing patient care, critical thinking, and delegation. Prerequisite: NURS 401; NURS 405; and NCLIN 407.

Course: PSYCLN 576 - Independent Study in Cognitive Science
Credits: 5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Provides students with a broad overview of the field of cognitive science. Designed to increase student knowledge base and to facilitate the integration of concepts, methods, and scientific findings in cognitive science into their scientific and clinical activities. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: B ECON 499 - Undergraduate Research
Credits: 1-6, max. 9
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Research in selected areas of business economics.

Course: NEURL 661 - P-Introduction to Neurology - Tacoma/Puyallup Multicare
Credits: 8
General Education: 
Prerequisites: completion of one required clerkship in medicine, family medicine, surgery, or pediatrics.
Description: Provides the medical student with a general understanding of basic clinical neurology at Neurology and Neurosurgery Associates in Tacoma and Puyallup, Washington. Students spend time at both clinics. Prerequisite: completion of one required clerkship in medicine, family medicine, surgery, or pediatrics.

Course: CM 429 - Construction Superintendent
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: CM 333 and CM 343. Offered: A.
Description: Study of the role and responsibilities of the Project Superintendent, analytical and technical skill sets used in managing field operations. Special emphasis on logistics, work flow planning, productivity tracking and development and management of a project schedule's critical
path. Prerequisite: CM 333 and CM 343. Offered: A.

Course: ORTHO 563 - Orthodontic Theory
Credits: 2
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Lecture-seminar sequence dealing with interpretation and application of orthodontic principles and concepts. Pertinent literature, research findings, and current orthodontic theory are analyzed in depth. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: M E 495 - Capstone Design II
Credits: -3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: M E 494. Offered: Sp.
Description: A continuation of M E 494. Course content varies from year to year and is dependent on the design topic chosen for M E 494. Prerequisite: M E 494. Offered: Sp.

Course: ECE 320 - Foundations of Indigenous Early Learning and Development
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc, DIV
Prerequisites: None
Description: Explores the strengths and brilliance of Indigenous peoples, the community methods for fostering positive child development, and articulating a vision of a just, sustainable world. Cultivates the skill of ongoing reflective practice through a social transformation lens. Explores strategies for teachers to support children and families from Indigenous communities by adopting land and water education approaches that expand upon community lifeways.

Course: FRENCH 102 - Elementary French
Credits: 5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: either FRENCH 101 or score of 15-30 on FR TL placement test.
Description: Development of speaking, listening, reading, and writing skills to a basic level of proficiency. Teaches students to communicate in French and understand the cultural context of the language. Methods and objectives are primarily oral-aural. Oral practice in the language laboratory is required. Second in a sequence of three. Maximum 15 credits allowed between FRENCH 101; FRENCH 102; FRENCH 103 (or equivalents); and FRENCH 134. Course equivalent to: BFRNCH 102. Course overlaps with: FRENCH 110. Prerequisite: either FRENCH 101 or score of 15-30 on FR TL placement test.

Course: MODHEB 199 - Study Abroad
Credits: 1-15, max. 15
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Credit for elementary Hebrew in an approved Study Abroad program. Requires credit evaluation by department or faculty. Does not automatically apply to major or minor requirements. Course overlaps with: BIBHEB 199.

Course: JEW ST 359 - Jewish American Literature and Culture
Credits: 5
General Education: A&H/SSc, DIV
Prerequisites: None
Description: Examines literary and cultural production about the Jewish experience in America. Considers ways in which American Jews assimilate and resist assimilation while Jewish writers, filmmakers, comedians, and graphic novelists imitate and transform American life and literature. Emphasizes questions of immigration, identity, gender, sexuality, race, inter-generational trauma, and cultural memory.

Course: SNKRT 202 - Intermediate Sanskrit
Credits: 5
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: SNKRT 201 Offered: W.
Description: Further study of classical grammar; introduction to classical literature and Vedic language and texts. Second in a sequence of three. Prerequisite: SNKRT 201 Offered: W.

Course: SOC 375 - Sociology of Juvenile Justice
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Overviews the United States juvenile justice system and related societal issues, including racial and ethnic disproportionality, the criminalization of delinquent offenders, and the future of the juvenile justice system.

Course: BIO A 100 - Evolution and Human Behavior
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc/NSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduction to evolution by natural selection, examining the light it can throw on human biology and behavior in such areas as the nature of sex differences, sexual conflict, and conflict between parents and children. Offered: jointly with BIOL 108.

Course: BIOEN 217 - MATLAB Fundamentals for Bioengineers
Credits: 1
General Education: 
Prerequisites: either CSE 121, CSE 122, CSE 123, CSE 142, CSE 160, or AMATH 301. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AW.
Description: Introduction to scientific programming, using both standard programming methods and MATLAB-specific strategies.  Intended as preparation for the Bioengineering core sequence.  Applications include curve fitting, simulations, ODE solutions, and image processing fundamentals, executed as in-class tutorials and final project. Prerequisite: either CSE 121, CSE 122, CSE 123, CSE 142, CSE 160, or AMATH 301. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AW.

Course: SEFS 554 - Wildlife Seminar
Credits: 1-2, max. 10
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Discussion of current research and application in wildlife biology and conservation. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.

Course: LSJ 444 - Ethics in Law and Justice
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Applies ethical theories, research, and practice to the law and justice system, with the goals of: (1) analyzing the moral dimensions of criminal law; (2) studying ethical issues in law enforcement, adjudications, and corrections; and (3) examining a variety of controversial ethical issues associated with the justice system.

Course: BIOEN 315 - Biochemical Molecular Engineering
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: CHEM 223, CHEM 237 or CHEM 335; BIOL 200, which may be taken concurrently. Offered: Sp.
Description: Introduces the requisite organic, physical, and biochemistry for incoming bioengineers to understand biological systems at the molecular level. Prerequisite: CHEM 223, CHEM 237 or CHEM 335; BIOL 200, which may be taken concurrently. Offered: Sp.

Course: JEW ST 302 - Jewish Experiences in World Literature and Cinema
Credits: 5
General Education: A&H, DIV
Prerequisites: None
Description: Explores the diversity of Jewish experiences through the study of literature, film, and graphic novels from around the world. Covers issues of tradition and secularization, diasporas and homelands; questions of cultural, racial, and sexual identities; effects of enormous changes wrought by displacements, world wars, the Holocaust, and other rapid cultural transformations. Course overlaps with: MELC 317/JEW ST 318. Offered: jointly with JSIS B 302.

Course: AIS 275 - Introductory Topics in American Indian and Indigenous Studies
Credits: 1-5, max. 15
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Covers introductory topics on current research and readings in American Indian and indigenous studies.

Course: ASTR 423 - High-Energy Astrophysics
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: PHYS 224; PHYS 225.
Description: High-energy phenomena in the universe. Includes supernova, pulsars, neutron stars, x-ray and gamma-ray sources, black holes, cosmic rays, quasi stellar objects, active galactic nuclei, diffuse background radiations. Radiative emission, absorption processes, and models derived from observational data. Prerequisite: PHYS 224; PHYS 225.

Course: UROL 680 - P-Urology Clerkship
Credits: *, max. 8
General Education: 
Prerequisites: HUBIO 562.
Description: Full activities of clinical service. Basic principles of urology emphasized. (Two or four weeks). Prerequisite: HUBIO 562.

Course: C MED 499 - Undergraduate Laboratory Research
Credits: 1-6, max. 12
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Specific problems in comparative medicine. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: JAPAN 441 - The Acquisition of Japanese as a Second or Foreign Language
Credits: 5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: either JAPAN 203, JAPAN 213, any 300-level JAPAN course, or any 400-level JAPAN course (any of which may be taken concurrently); and either JAPAN 343, JAPAN 344, ASIAN 401, CHIN 342, any 200-level LING course, or any 300-level LING course.
Description: Focuses on how Japanese is acquired or learned by non-native speakers in North America and Japan. Includes study of how Japanese is learned in both naturalistic settings such as study abroad and in foreign language classrooms. Prerequisite: either JAPAN 203, JAPAN 213, any 300-level JAPAN course, or any 400-level JAPAN course (any of which may be taken concurrently); and either JAPAN 343, JAPAN 344, ASIAN 401, CHIN 342, any 200-level LING course, or any 300-level LING course.

Course: LSJ 401 - Field Experience in Law, Societies, and Justice
Credits: 5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Participant observation in a public or private agency relevant to the study of law, justice, human rights, or court systems.

Course: URDU 423 - Advanced Urdu Fourth Year: The Novel
Credits: 5, max. 15
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: two of the following courses: URDU 321, URDU 322, or URDU 323.
Description: Surveys the development of the novel in Urdu, with readings of representative texts and discussion of their historical and cultural contexts. Prerequisite: two of the following courses: URDU 321, URDU 322, or URDU 323.

Course: ARCTIC 391 - Climate Change - An International Perspective: Science, Art, and Activism
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc/A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Explores climate change science in the context of geographic, social, and political constraints, considering the role of art, activism, and Arctic indigenous peoples in communicating impacts and mitigation. Students gain knowledge in key atmospheric and ocean science principles along with the role of science in society Offered: jointly with JSIS B 391; Sp.

Course: RUSS 520 - Topics in Russian Literature and Culture
Credits: 5, max. 20
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Detailed study of a single author or a movement, theme, or short period in Russian literature or culture.

Course: ASTR 400 - Undergraduate Research Seminar
Credits: 1
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduces research topics conducted by astronomy faculty. Each week a faculty member describes her/his current research and the opportunities available for interested majors to participate in the research. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: A.

Course: MSE 587 - Composites Engineering, Production, and Maintenance
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Provides overview of composite materials and processes. Covers how the unique characteristics of composites are accommodated in the disciplines and practices of engineering, production, and maintenance to assure composite structural part integrity throughout the product life cycle.

Course: LING 572 - Advanced Statistical Methods in Natural Language Processing
Credits: 4
General Education: 
Prerequisites: LING 570. Offered: W.
Description: Covers several important machine learning algorithms for natural language processing including decision tree, kNN, Naive Bayes, transformation-based learning, support vector machine, maximum entropy, and conditional random field. Students implement many of the algorithms and apply these algorithms to some NLP tasks. Prerequisite: LING 570. Offered: W.

Course: MUSICP 315 - Private Instruction for Non-Majors: Tuba
Credits: 2, max. 44
General Education: A&H
Prerequisites: None
Description: Intended for undergraduate non-majors. Audition required.

Course: NEUR S 655 - P-Clinical Neurosurgery Clerkship- Spokane WA
Credits: 1-8, max. 8
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Provides the medical student with exposure to common neurologic and neurosurgical problems such as trauma, hydrocephalus, stroke, back pain, bleeds in the head, and tumors. Satisfies the requirement of the Neurology clerkship requirement. For third- and fourth-year medical students. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: CET 591 - Freight Transportation
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Overview of the technical and institutional aspects of transporting freight. Topics include the different modes of moving freight, the technology of transferring freight between modes at ports and terminals, issues that impact freight movement such as congestion and government regulation, and the future of freight mobility. Also covers regional freight demand modeling techniques. Offered: A.

Course: JSIS B 440 - The Communist Experience Around the World
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Communism from its origins in Bolshevik faction of Russian social democracy to the present, treating the development of the ideology, the various communist parties, and the communist states. Offered: jointly with HSTCMP 440.

Course: ESS 507 - High-Temperature Geochemistry
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduces quantitative high-temperature geochemistry. Focuses on understanding the fundamentals of geochemical processes. Examines the application of quantitative geochemical tools to investigate these processes. Processes covered include: accretion and differentiation of the solar system, continental formation and evolution, subduction zone processes, mantle heterogeneity, mass extinctions and Snowball Earth, and atmospheric evolution. Recommended: ESS 212 or ESS 316.

Course: GWSS 298 - Study Abroad: Introductory Topics
Credits: 1-10, max. 15
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Courses taken through a UW approved study abroad program that align with gender, women, and sexuality studies topics. Content varies and must be individually evaluated.

Course: PHRMSC 313 - Drug Disposition and Delivery
Credits: 3
General Education: NSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduces the principles of pharmaceutics, drug disposition, drug delivery, and related concepts in the pharmaceutical sciences. Recommended: basic knowledge of general chemistry; anatomy; and physiology. Offered: A.

Course: IMT 585 - Program Management and Consulting
Credits: 4
General Education: 
Prerequisites: IMT 580.
Description: Provides overview of skills, practices, and concepts foundational to a career in information management consulting. Topics include consulting concepts, methodologies, approaches to consultative analysis and problem solving, effective technical and interpersonal consulting behaviors, and program management in a consulting environment. Emphasizes interpersonal/communication skills, client relationship management, and change management. Prerequisite: IMT 580.

Course: LIS 578 - Research Seminar
Credits: 1-4, max. 10
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Students work in teams under the supervision of individual faculty members to engage in research or design activities and learn through hands-on participation and study. Learning activities include data collection, data analysis, building prototypes, testing or evaluation, or dissemination activities. Course equivalent to: IMT 578.

Course: A A 461 - Air Breathing Propulsion
Credits: 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: A A 460. Offered: W.
Description: Examines gas turbine engine design methodology. Covers aerodynamics or gas dynamics of air breathing engine components: inlets, compressors, turbines, and nozzles. Studies the on-design and off-design performance of gas turbine engines. Includes combustion, emissions, noise, and advanced air breathing propulsion systems. Prerequisite: A A 460. Offered: W.

Course: ARAB 411 - Arabic through Song
Credits: 5
General Education: A&H/SSc
Prerequisites: either ARAB 203 or ARAB 205.
Description: Emphasizes history, language, and culture explored, learned, and analyzed via songs. Considers how song reflects and portrays language and its usage; current and past events; and cultural nuances. Prerequisite: either ARAB 203 or ARAB 205.

Course: SOC WF 200 - Introduction to Social Welfare Practice
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc
Prerequisites: None
Description: Introduction to the field of social work, including the theoretical concepts and institutional framework that guide practice. Overview of social work profession and social welfare system within which it operates. Lectures supplemented by exercises, films, guest lectures, and class discussions. Offered: A.

Course: A A 499 - Undergraduate Research
Credits: 1-5, max. 10
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Research on special topics under the supervision of a faculty member. Application of fundamentals learned in the classroom to real problems in research. A maximum of 6 credits may be applied toward senior technical electives. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: JSIS 196 - Study Abroad: Latin American and Caribbean Studies
Credits: 1-5, max. 15

Description: For participants in study abroad program. Specific course content varies. Courses do not automatically apply to major/minor requirements.

Course: COM 489 - Black Cultural Studies
Credits: 5
General Education: SSc, DIV
Prerequisites: None
Description: Examines how images of blackness have been (re)constructed through identity formation and entrenched inequality. Topics include black women's bodies, black men's bodies, blackface minstrelsy, black queer studies, black power, and black hybridities. Offered: jointly with AES 489/GWSS 489.

Course: COM 576 - Interpersonal Communication
Credits: 5
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Social scientific research and theory on the role of communication in developing and maintaining interpersonal relationships. Nature of interpersonal communication, relationship change processes, interpersonal control through communication, and personal communication networks.

Course: LAB M 600 - Independent Study or Research
Credits: *-
General Education: 
Prerequisites: graduate standing in laboratory medicine. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSpS.
Description: Prerequisite: graduate standing in laboratory medicine. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSpS.

Course: PEDO 575 - Pediatric Dentistry Seminar VI
Credits: 2
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Principles and theory of child development and behavior management for pediatric patient. Sedation, general anesthesia, and principles of informed consent, pathology of oral manifestations of diseases of children and adolescents, pediatric radiology, and use of computers in didactic, clinical, and research endeavors, and the scientific basis for  prevention and treatment of dental caries, periodontal disease, and developmental anomalies. Offered: A.

Course: SPAN 562 - Twentieth-Century Latin American Literature and Culture
Credits: 5, max. 20
General Education: 
Prerequisites: None
Description: Twentieth-century Latin American cultural production. Focus on literature, music, and visual arts. Includes such topics as inter-artistic relations, cultural responses to social and political movements, and influences of mass media technologies and popular culture. Offered: Sp.

Course: DENTCP 680 - Endodontics Clinic
Credits: 1-, max. 3
General Education: 
Prerequisites: all preclinical coursework and DENTCL 620. Offered: AWSp.
Description: Students perform diagnosis, treatment planning, and endodontic therapy for cases of minimal difficulty within the scope of general dentistry. Learning experiences include assisting peers and graduate students in patient care and completing clinical simulation exercises to strengthen endodontic skills. Prerequisite: all preclinical coursework and DENTCL 620. Offered: AWSp.

Course: MGMT 430 - Strategic Management
Credits: 4
General Education: 
Prerequisites: FIN 350; MKTG 301; either HRMOB 300 or MGMT 300.
Description: Develops strategic thinking skills for balancing opportunities and risks of business competition to generate superior value for stakeholders. Performs in-depth analyses of industries and competitors, predicts competitive behavior, and explores how firms develop and sustain competitive advantage over time. Prerequisite: FIN 350; MKTG 301; either HRMOB 300 or MGMT 300.

Course: EDPSY 595 - Monte Carlo Simulations
Credits: 3

Course: PHRMCY 541 - Pharmacist Provider Readiness I
Credits: 4
General Education:
